messages:
Maria: heads-up — noticed a spike in 5xxs and 413s from /v1/embeddings around 09:22 UTC.
Sam: ok what payloads? any common pattern?
Maria: customers sending mixed-dim arrays in a single request. e.g. one document with 1536-d vectors and another with 768-d in the same "inputs" array.
Maria: splitter tried to route by byte size, ended up sending the batch to CPU-only fallback which timed out under load.
Kevin: ugh. we treat embeddings as homogeneous dims at runtime, but the client contract isn't enforced strictly.
Clair: do we have preflight validation? I thought console preflight would surface this.
Maria: we have a lightweight preflight in the console but it doesn't run in the hosted API path. the router only sees the raw body and tries to chunk by size.
Sam: can we detect mixed dims cheaply? read first 64 bytes to infer dims header? but many clients send raw arrays without a header.
Leah: proposal: require an explicit header `X-Embedding-Dim` (int) when `inputs` contains arrays, else run a fast scan and reject if mixed. reject early with 422 and a helpful message. cheaper than routing wrong.
Kevin: seems reasonable. two concerns: (1) breaking clients that send mixed by accident, (2) overhead for large batches if we scan everything.
Maria: breaking clients is ok if we do a graceful rollout + docs. we can also support a `mixed_dims=true` query flag to opt-in to mixed handling which routes to the safer slow-path.
Sam: another idea: preflight that computes dims summary (count per-dim) and emits telemetry to console so customers see their bad payloads before we enforce.
Clair: +1 for telemetry. add a soft-reject mode for 48h that returns 200 with a `warnings` array in body and a header `X-Embed-Warn: mixed-dims` so we don't surprise prod systems.
Leah: rollout plan:
- soft-detect + telemetry (console) -> 48h
- soft-reject with warnings -> 72h
- enforce 422 unless `mixed_dims=true` -> then route to slow-path
- last: deprecate slow-path after 30d if adoption is good
Sam: implementation notes: router needs a fast preflight that only samples first N vectors (N configurable, default 8). that'll avoid scanning huge payloads.
Kevin: also add a metric `embed.mixed_dims.requests` with labels {route, account, sampled=true/false} to track.
Maria: need PRs:
- eng-platform: router preflight + sampling (sam)
- eng-runtime: slow-path route improvements + quota handling (kevin)
- devex/docs: console warnings + UX copy (clair)
- support/ops: run a query to find accounts that send mixed dims last 7d (leah)
Sam: I'll open the router PR today and include the sampling hook + opt-in query param.
Kevin: I'll add the telemetry events and make the slow-path return a clear `X-Embed-Route: cpu-fallback` header when used.
Clair: I'll draft console banner text: "Mixed-dimension payloads may be rejected soon — enable mixed_dims=true for temporary fallback" and a link to migration guide.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: router-preflight-sampling -> canary in us-west-2 at 2026-03-22T02:00Z
ops-bot: alert created: #incidents to watch for `embed.*5xx` spikes during canary
Maria: testcases:
- 1 batch homogeneous 1536 -> pass
- 1 batch mixed [1536,768] -> soft-warning then 422
- streaming chunked upload -> sample across chunks
- large N=1000 batch -> sampling must be bounded
Sam: noted. will include unit + e2e mocks for splitter.
Leah: also add a console telemetry card that surfaces top offending accounts and example payload (redacted) so SEs can reach out.
Kevin: timeline looks fine. I'll prioritize telemetry so we can see the impact before hard enforcing.
Maria: thanks team. follow-up in #eng-platform tomorrow with links to PRs and console previews.
Clair: cc @Support for outreach once we flip enforcement.
Sam: PR 4201 opened: router preflight sampling + mixed_dims param -> https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4201 :eyes:
Maria: will review today.
Leah: I'll run the historical query and DM top 10 accounts.
Maria: milestone: aim to start soft-reject 2026-03-29 if telemetry looks sane.
Kevin: copy. any objections -> speak now or in PR review.
